Bernard Faried Lewis''' ({{IPAc-en|f|ə|r|ˈ|iː|d}} {{respell|fə|REED}}; born November 19, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Known as "'''the Manimal'''" due to his hustle on the court, he attended [[Morehead State University]] for four years, twice being named the [[Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ohio Valley Conference Player of the Year]].{{cite web|first=Benjamin|last=Hochman|title=Nuggets rookie Faried lives up to "Manimal" nickname|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2011/12/11/nuggets-rookie-faried-lives-up-to-manimal-nickname/|work=The Denver Post|date=December 11, 2011|access-date=June 17, 2020}} He finished his collegiate career as the [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball career rebounding leaders|NCAA all-time leading rebounder]] in the [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball career rebounding leaders#Post-1973 era|post-1973 era]] with 1,673 rebounds, although he was surpassed by [[Armando Bacot]] in 2024. He was selected 22nd overall in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]]. Faried played for the [[United States national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], where he won a gold medal and was named to the All-Tournament Team. ==High school career== Faried attended [[Technology High School (New Jersey)|Technology High School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]].{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/03/17/sports/ncaabasketball/17morehead.html?_r=0 | work=The New York Times | first=John | last=Branch | title=Morehead State Star Faried Leaves Trouble Behind | date=March 16, 2011}}{{cite news | url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=6101092 | title=Kenneth Faried adapts and thrives | first=Dana | last=O'Neil | work=[[ESPN.com]] | date=February 9, 2011 | access-date=March 20, 2011}}{{Cite web |last=Star-Ledger |first=Zach Berman/The |date=2011-06-22 |title=With NBA Draft in his hometown, Newark native Kenneth Faried will see dream fulfilled |url=https://www.nj.com/nets/2011/06/at_nba_draft_in_his_hometown_n.html |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=nj |language=en}} Due to his lanky physique and low standardized test scores, he was not heavily recruited out of high school, only receiving interest from [[Iona College (New York)|Iona College]], [[Marist College]], and [[Morehead State University]].{{Cite web|date=2011-02-09|title=O'Neil: Morehead State's Faried doesn't do conventional|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=6101092|access-date=2020-06-19|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} He ultimately chose to attend Morehead State, citing their persistence as the deciding factor.{{Cite news|last=Raskin|first=Alex|date=2011-06-02|title=Could He Be the Next Rodman?|language=en-US|work=Wall Street Journal|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303657404576357620361233058|access-date=2020-06-19|issn=0099-9660}} ==College career== [[File:Ed Daniel.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Faried (hands up) with Morehead State in February 2011]] A {{height|ft=6|in=8}} post player, Faried arrived at [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State]] in 2007. He led the [[Ohio Valley Conference]] in [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] as both a sophomore and a junior (13.0 rebounds per game in each season) – ranking him third in the [[NCAA Division I|NCAA]] in [[2008–09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2008–09]] and second in [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]]. Faried also chipped in double-digit scoring in each of his three varsity seasons.{{Cite web |title=Kenneth Faried - Men's Basketball |url=https://msueagles.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kenneth-faried/1433 |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=Morehead State University Athletics |language=en}} Faried also led the Eagles to team success, as Morehead claimed a berth in the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009 NCAA tournament]] by winning the [[2009 Ohio Valley Conference men's basketball tournament|Ohio Valley Conference tournament]]. He led the way in the conference championship, his 15 points and 17 rebounds in its final against [[Austin Peay Governors basketball|Austin Peay]] earning him the tournament's [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]]. In his junior year Faried again led the Eagles to the post-season, as they advanced to the second round of the [[2010 College Basketball Invitational|College Basketball Invitational]]. At the end of the season, Faried was named OVC Player and Defensive Player of the Year and an [[Associated Press|AP]] honorable mention [[2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].{{Cite web |date=2010-03-29 |title=Faried Named AP All-America Honorable Mention |url=https://msueagles.com/news/2010/3/29/MBB_0329101455.aspx?path=mbball |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=Morehead State University Athletics |language=en}} He also passed 1000 rebounds for his career. After his junior season, Faried declared himself eligible for the [[2010 NBA draft]]. However, he elected to return as a senior,{{Cite web |title=Morehead State's Faried to Return For Senior Season |url=http://ovcsports.com/news/2010/5/7/5480.aspx |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=ovcsports.com |language=en}} and went on to break [[Tim Duncan]]'s modern-era (post-1973) Division I career rebounding record of 1,570 rebounds. The mark, which had stood since 1997, fell to Faried's 12 rebounds in the Eagles' 71–65 victory over [[2010–11 Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball team|Indiana State]] on February 19, 2011. [[2010–11 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]] again won the [[2011 Ohio Valley Conference men's basketball tournament|Ohio Valley conference tournament]], earning a 13 seed in the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011 NCAA tournament]]. Led by the play of Faried, Morehead State pulled off a huge upset in the first round of the tournament, toppling the 4 seed [[2010–11 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville Cardinals]]. Faried ended his collegiate career with [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball career rebounding leaders#Post-1973 era|1,673 rebounds]]. In his senior season, Faried was named a second-team [[2011 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] and [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].{{cite news|first=Jeff |last=Goodman |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 leader (1,673 rebounds) (post-1973) ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets (2011–2018)=== [[File:Lakers vs Nuggets 2013-01-06 (7).JPG|thumb|left|Faried with the Nuggets in January 2013]] On June 23, 2011, Faried was selected by the [[Denver Nuggets]] with the 22nd overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/players/kenneth/faried/202702|title=Kenneth Faried stats, details, videos, and news.|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 4, 2018}} Prior to his rookie season, he earned the nickname "Manimal", for playing hard and fearlessly.{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2011/12/14/kenneth-faried-nuggets-rookie-on-denver-dennis-rodman-and-being-a-manimal/|title=Kenneth Faried: Nuggets' rookie on Denver, Dennis Rodman and being a "Manimal"|work=denverpost.com|date=December 14, 2011|access-date=October 4, 2018}} He appeared in 46 games (39 starts) in his rookie year, recording 10.2 points and 7.7 rebounds per game in 22.5 minutes. He posted career highs of 27 points and 17 rebounds against the [[Golden State Warriors]] on April 9, 2012, becoming the first player in the shot-clock era to have at least 27 points and 17 rebounds while playing less than 25 minutes. He went on to be named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for April.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/faried_named_western_conference.html|title=Faried Named Western Conference Rookie of the Month|work=NBA.com|date=April 27, 2012|access-date=October 4, 2018}} He finished third in [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] voting for the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]],{{cite web|url=http://pr.nba.com/kyrie-irving-2011-12-kia-nba-rookie-of-the-year/|title=Cavaliers' Kyrie Irving named 2011-12 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year|work=NBA.com|date=May 15, 2012|access-date=October 4, 2018}} and earned [[NBA All-Rookie Team]] honors.{{cite web|last=Kay|first=Alex|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1192378-2012-nba-all-rookie-team-kyrie-irving-headlines-released-roster|title=2012 NBA All-Rookie Team: Kyrie Irving Headlines Roster|work=bleacherreport.com|date=May 23, 2012|access-date=October 4, 2018}} On November 12, 2012, Faried was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, November 5, through Sunday, November 11. It was his first and only player of the week award of his career.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/11/12/lebron-james-kenneth-faried-players-of-week/|title=James, Faried named conference Players of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=November 12, 2012|access-date=October 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131209105404/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/11/12/lebron-james-kenneth-faried-players-of-week/|archive-date=December 9, 2013|url-status=dead}} Three days later, he posted 16 points and a career-high 20 rebounds (career-high 11 offensive) in 36 minutes against the [[Miami Heat]]. On December 12, he recorded a season-high 26 points, 14 rebounds and career-high three steals in 38 minutes against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. On February 15, 2013, he was named MVP of the [[Rising Stars Challenge]], where he recorded 40 points and 10 rebounds in 22 minutes for the winning side as Team Chuck beat Team Shaq 163–135.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130215/SHQCHK/gameinfo.html|title=Team Shaq at Team Chuck|work=NBA.com|date=February 15, 2013|access-date=October 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130216065615/http://www.nba.com/games/20130215/SHQCHK/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 16, 2013|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/news/as.rising.stars/2013-rising-stars-challenge-event-page/|title=Faried grabs MVP as Team Chuck wins BBVA Rising Stars|work=NBA.com|date=February 16, 2013|access-date=October 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180713012709/http://www.nba.com/news/as.rising.stars/2013-rising-stars-challenge-event-page/|archive-date=July 13, 2018|url-status=dead}} He also competed in the 2013 [[Slam Dunk Contest|Sprite Slam Dunk Contest]], but was eliminated in the team round. On February 3, 2014, Faried recorded a career-high 28 points to go along with 11 rebounds against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He registered a new career high with 32 points on 14-of-20 shooting and grabbed 13 rebounds against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on March 7. He posted 34 points and grabbed 13 rebounds in 27 minutes on April 2 against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]],{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140402/NOPDEN/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Nuggets 137, Pelicans 107|work=NBA.com|date=April 2, 2014|access-date=October 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140422024853/http://www.nba.com/games/20140402/NOPDEN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 22, 2014|url-status=dead}} becoming the first player in NBA history to record those numbers while playing 27 minutes or less. He recorded 24 points to go along with a career-high 21 rebounds against the [[Utah Jazz]] on April 12. On October 8, 2014, Faried signed a multi-year contract extension with the Nuggets.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/nuggets-sign-kenneth-faried-multiyear-contract-extension|title=Nuggets sign Kenneth Faried to multiyear contract extension|work=NBA.com|date=October 8, 2014|access-date=October 4, 2018}} On December 26, he had a career-high 25 rebounds to go along with 26 points, as the Nuggets beat the Timberwolves 106–102.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141226/MINDEN/gameinfo.html|title=Faried grabs 25 rebounds as Denver beats Minnesota 106-102|work=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2014|access-date=October 4, 2018}} On April 12, 2015, he scored a season-high 30 points in a 122–111 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150412/SACDEN/gameinfo.html|title=Faried scores 30 points, Nuggets beat Kings 122-111|work=NBA.com|date=April 12, 2015|access-date=October 4, 2018}} On November 3, 2015, Faried scored a season-high 28 points in a 120–109 win over the Lakers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151103/DENLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Faried leads Nuggets' surge past winless Lakers, 120-109|work=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2015|access-date=October 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160111033815/http://www.nba.com/games/20151103/DENLAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 11, 2016|url-status=dead}} On March 6, 2016, he recorded 25 points and a season-high 20 rebounds in a 116–114 overtime win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160306/DALDEN/gameinfo.html|title=Augustin's free throws lift Nuggets over Mavs in OT, 116-114|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2016|access-date=October 4, 2018}} Faried suffered through a sore back for much of the 2016–17 season and caused him to miss 15 games overall, most of which were in February, March and the final games in April. He played through the pain in many others. He played in 61 games overall with averages of 9.6 points and 7.5 rebounds in 21.2 minutes, all career lows.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/profile-1617/faried|title=2016-17 Player Profile: Kenneth Faried|work=NBA.com|date=May 8, 2017|access-date=October 4, 2018}} Faried's role shifted to the bench over his final two years in Denver, especially after the Nuggets traded for [[Mason Plumlee]] and signed NBA All-Star [[Paul Millsap]] and reserve [[Trey Lyles]] as the backup [[Power Forward]] in 2017.{{cite web|url=https://thednvr.com/once-the-forgotten-man-in-denvers-frontcourt-kenneth-faried-again-proves-his-worth/|title=Once the Forgotten Man in Denver's Frontcourt, Kenneth Faried Again Proves His Worth|work=thednvr.com|date=October 22, 2017|access-date=June 25, 2026}} Displeased, Faried insisted that he is "not a bench player" and that he is "a starter".{{cite web|url=https://milehighsports.com/kenneth-faried-expresses-unhappiness-with-not-starting/|title=Kenneth Faried's Insistence on Starting Sends Ominous Message to Nuggets|work=Mile High Sports|date=September 25, 2017|access-date=June 25, 2026}} With Faried's role diminishing in the [[2017–18 NBA season]], he averaged career lows of 5.9 points and 4.8 rebounds per contest in just 32 games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/07/13/report-denver-nuggets-ship-kenneth-faried-darrell-arthur-future-pick-brooklyn|title=Reports: Denver Nuggets send Kenneth Faried, Darrell Arthur, future pick to Brooklyn Nets|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2018|access-date=October 4, 2018}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2018–2019)=== On July 13, 2018, Faried was traded, along with [[Darrell Arthur]], a protected 2019 first-round draft pick and a 2020 second-round draft pick, to his hometown team the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Isaiah Whitehead]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/07/13/brooklyn-nets-acquire-kenneth-faried-darrell-arthur-denver-nuggets|title=Brooklyn Nets acquire Kenneth Faried, Darrell Arthur from Denver Nugget|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2018|access-date=July 13, 2018}} On January 19, 2019, he was waived by the Nets.{{cite Kenneth Faried is a committed [[straight ally]], having worked with the [[GLAAD|Gay and Lesbian Alliance Against Defamation (GLAAD)]] and also with [[Athlete Ally]], a group that works to break down homophobia in sports.{{cite web |title=Kenneth Faried makes moms proud |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/e60/story/_/id/9248194/denver-nuggets-kenneth-faried-makes-mothers-proud |website=ESPN.com |access-date=May 31, 2023 |date=May 6, 2013}} Faried has at least four children, including three sons and one daughter.{{cite web |title='I had to seek therapy': what happens when an NBA career ends before its time? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2023/apr/05/i-had-to-seek-therapy-what-happens-when-an-nba-career-ends-before-its-time |website=The Guardian |date=5 April 2023 |access-date=18 November 2025}}{{cite web |title=3BOYS (KT, Kenai & Kiyan) & 2GIRLS (Kyra & Kenzie) & 1 Wifie @wishuponatar |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CQZJac5jWAK/ |website=Instagram |access-date=18 November 2025}} His social-media profile with his partner, Atar Hajali, names three sons (KT, Kenai, and Kiyan) and two daughters (Kyra and Kenzie). ==See also== {{Portal|Sports}} * [[List of NBA career field goal percentage leaders]] * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season rebounding leaders]] * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball career rebounding leaders]] * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball players with 2,000 points and 1,000 rebounds]] ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{commons}} {{basketballstats|nba=202702|bbr=f/farieke01}} *[http://www.msueagles.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1433&path=mbball Morehead State Eagles bio] {{Saski Baskonia current roster}} {{Navboxes|list= {{2011 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{NABC Defensive Player of the Year}} {{Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{NCAA Division I men's basketball rebounding champion}} {{2011 NBA draft}} {{J.
